inline_comments.comment: The magic number `27` appears in two places: as the parameter default on line 311 and as the fallback inside the `limit` ternary on line 338. If the default ever needs to change, both spots must be updated in sync. Extract a single module-level constant (e.g. `const DEFAULT_MAX_PRESET_COLORS = 27`) and reference it from both locations.

None of the three new stories (`WithMaxPresetColors`, `WithUnlimitedPresetColors`, `WithInvalidMaxPresetColors`) include a `play` function with DOM assertions. Since the color picker is opened via `startOpen: true`, it is straightforward to query the rendered swatches and assert the correct count. For example, `WithMaxPresetColors` should assert that exactly 5 swatches are present, and `WithUnlimitedPresetColors` should assert that all 40 are rendered. Without these assertions the stories act only as visual demos and provide no automated regression protection for the new feature.

general_comments.comment: The `maxPresetColors` parameter is typed as `number`, which also permits `NaN`. `NaN === 0` and `NaN === Infinity` are both false, and `Number.isInteger(NaN)` is false, so the code silently falls back to 27 — which is arguably acceptable, but callers receive no indication that their value was invalid. Consider either narrowing the type (e.g. a branded positive-integer type, though TypeScript makes this difficult) or adding an explicit guard and a `console.warn` for values that are not positive integers, not `0`, and not `Infinity`, so developers are alerted to misconfiguration during development.
